executive_summary.text: Interpol's Operation First Light nets 5,800 cybercrime arrests across 97 countries with $293M seized—largest global law enforcement action against online fraud.
GigaWiper destructive backdoor combines ransomware and wiper capabilities, targeting critical infrastructure.

cyber_news.title: WolfSSL, GeoVision, VTK vulnerabilities
cyber_news.summary: Cisco Talos' Vulnerability Discovery & Research team recently disclosed three vulnerabilities in WolfSSL, fourteen in GeoVision, and one vulnerability in VTK-DICOM.
cyber_news.expanded: Cisco Talos discovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in WolfSSL (14 in GeoVision, 1 in VTK-DICOM). WolfSSL is widely used in IoT, embedded systems, and critical infrastructure. Vulnerabilities range from buffer overflows to authentication bypasses, enabling remote code execution on affected devices.

cyber_news.title: Microsoft Patches RoguePlanet Defender Flaw That Can Grant SYSTEM Privileges
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft addresses critical privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Defender.
cyber_news.expanded: RoguePlanet privilege escalation flaw in Windows Defender allowed unprivileged processes to elevate to SYSTEM level. Attack leveraged Windows service interactions. Patch released immediately; exploitation in the wild detected. Critical for organizations relying on Defender for endpoint protection.

cyber_news.title: 15-Year-Old Linux Vulnerability 'GhostLock' Earns Researchers $92k From Google
cyber_news.summary: Affecting every major Linux distribution since 2011, the kernel vulnerability allows attackers to gain root access.
cyber_news.expanded: Kernel vulnerability in Linux since 2011 affects all major distributions (Ubuntu, RHEL, Debian, etc.). Allows unprivileged user to gain root access through specific system call sequence. Google's vulnerability reward program assessed risk as critical; 15-year window of exposure indicates widespread affected systems.

cyber_news.title: GhostApproval Flaw Hits Six Major AI Coding Assistants
cyber_news.summary: Wiz discovered GhostApproval, a symlink flaw in six major AI coding assistants that bypasses approval workflows.
cyber_news.expanded: Symlink vulnerability in AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and others) allows threat actors to craft malicious repositories that bypass approval workflows. When developers review code, symlinks point to sensitive files, executing arbitrary commands with developer privileges. Attack chains can compromise CI/CD pipelines and development infrastructure.

cyber_news.title: New Forg365 phishing platform uses AI to target Microsoft 365 accounts
cyber_news.summary: AI-powered phishing platform specifically designed to compromise Microsoft 365 user credentials.
cyber_news.expanded: AI-powered phishing platform specifically targeting Microsoft 365 environments. Uses machine learning to craft convincing credential-harvesting sites. Threat actors automate mass campaigns against M365 user bases; increased success rate vs. traditional phishing.

cyber_news.title: Fake 7-Zip Installers Turn Devices Into Residential Proxy Nodes
cyber_news.summary: Malicious 7-Zip installers discovered distributing proxy malware to compromise residential networks.
cyber_news.expanded: Fake 7-Zip installers distributed via typosquatting and malicious ads. Once installed, malware converts compromised devices into residential proxy nodes, selling access to malicious actors. Supply chain attack leveraging trusted software distribution vectors.

cyber_news.summary: Survey reveals security concerns in European organizations regarding collaboration platform vulnerabilities.

deep_dive.title: Interpol cybercrime crackdown nets 5,800 arrests across 97 countries
deep_dive.content: Operation First Light, coordinated by Interpol across 97 countries, resulted in the arrest of 5,800 suspected cybercriminals and recovery of $293 million in seized assets. This multi-national law enforcement initiative targeted organized cybercrime networks engaged in fraud, ransomware operations, and financial crimes. The scale and coordination represent unprecedented global cooperation against transnational cybercriminal enterprises. Participating agencies leveraged intelligence sharing, real-time surveillance coordination, and simultaneous enforcement actions to prevent warning dissemination among criminal networks. Success required harmonized legal frameworks, extradition agreements, and technical capacity-sharing among nations with varying cybercrime prosecution infrastructure. The operation demonstrates law enforcement capability evolution in response to increasingly sophisticated and globally-distributed threat actors. Seized assets and arrested personnel disrupt criminal operations' financial flows and operational capacity, creating deterrent effects across multiple threat vectors.
